texts.li: {A_nameDef} has come to the council about {DEAD}, {DEED}. Some are already saying {SAINT}, {A_pronoun} says, and {A_pronoun} asks the council to say so too: name {DEAD} {ASAINT}, and let the grave be a place to pray.

[reason:rescuer] {A_nameDef} can't stop talking about how {DEAD} died, carrying someone out while the fighting was still going on. {A_pronoun} asks the council to name {DEAD} {ASAINT}, so the colony never forgets it.
[reason:defender] {DEAD} held the line until the end, and {A_nameDef} wants it remembered properly: {ASAINT}, {A_pronoun} says, with a day of {DEAD}'s own every year.
[reason:healer] Half the colony owes {DEAD} a life or a limb, {A_nameDef} says. {A_pronoun} asks the council to name {DEAD} {ASAINT}, and to let the sick pray at the grave.
[reason:keeper] {DEAD} kept faith longer and more surely than anyone here, {A_nameDef} says. {A_pronoun} asks the council to name {DEAD} {ASAINT}.
[reason:vow] {DEAD} died with a vow still being kept, {A_nameDef} says, and kept it to the very end. {A_pronoun} asks the council to name {DEAD} {ASAINT}.
[priest] It falls to the priest to ask, {A_nameDef} says: {DEAD}, {DEED}, should be named {ASAINT}, and the grave made a place to pray.

li.label: Name {DEAD} {ASAINT}
li.outcome: The council named {DEAD} {ASAINT}. {A_nameDef} said the words at the grave that evening, and those who came stayed a while after.

outcomes.li: [known] The council named {DEAD} {ASAINT}. {A_nameDef} said the words at the grave that evening, and someone left a candle there for {GOD}.

li.label: Honour {DEAD}, and go no further
li.outcome: The council would not go that far, but {A_nameDef} said a few words at the grave that evening, and nobody thought less of {DEAD} for it.

li.label: Let {DEAD} rest
li.outcome: The council let {DEAD} rest as {DEAD} was. {A_nameDef} took it quietly.

li.label: one of ours named a saint
li.description: The council named one of our own a saint. Whatever else happens, they'll be remembered here.

li.label: prayed to a saint
li.description: I said a few words at a saint's place. Someone who was one of us is listening, I'm sure of it.

li.label: prayed before a relic
li.description: I knelt before a saint's relic, as my faith teaches. It felt like they were in the room.

li.label: kept a saint's day
li.description: We kept a saint's day together. It's good to remember the ones who went before us.

JobDef.reportString: raising a statue to a saint.

ThingDef.label: saint's relic
ThingDef.description: A keepsake of one of the colony's own saints, set aside when the council named them: a lock of hair, a small bone, a worn token, whatever the colony keeps such things in. It is a place to pray to them wherever it lies, and a faith that keeps relics venerates it as one.

plain.li: {SAINT}, you knew this place, so keep an eye on it for us.
{SAINT}, it's me again, and we could use a little luck.
Remember us, {SAINT}, the way we remember you.
{SAINT}, I don't know if you can hear me, but I'm saying it anyway.
[known] {SAINT}, put in a word with {GOD} for us.
[known] Ask {GOD} to go easy on us this season, {SAINT}.
[known] You're closer to {GOD} than any of us now, {SAINT}, so tell it we're trying.
[place:grave] Rest easy, {SAINT}, we're still here and still trying.
[place:grave] I brought nothing but myself today, {SAINT}, I hope that's enough.
[place:statue] It doesn't look much like you, {SAINT}, but it's the thought that counts.
[place:relic] I'll keep this safe for you, {SAINT}, I promise.
[tribal] Ancestor, walk beside us when we go out past the fires.
[spacer] {SAINT}, if any part of you is out there, we're still listening.
A year ago today we lost {DEAD}, and we still haven't stopped talking about them.
{SAINT}, {DEED}, is why we're all standing here tonight.
Say {DEAD}'s name, everyone, so the ground knows we haven't forgotten.
We keep {SAINT}'s day so that whoever comes after us keeps it too.
If you're new here, ask anyone about {DEAD}, they'll tell you.
[known] {SAINT} walks with {GOD} now, and puts in a word for us.
[known] {GOD} took {DEAD} home, and we keep the day for both of them.
[tribal] The fire is lit for {SAINT}, so the Ancestors can find their way here tonight.
[spacer] We kept {DEAD}'s voice, and tonight we let it speak again.
From today this stands for {SAINT}, and anyone may pray here.
This is {SAINT}'s now, so treat it kindly.
Let this be {SAINT}'s, for as long as it stands.
[known] For {SAINT}, and for {GOD} who keeps them.
The council has spoken, and from today we call them by a holier name.
They were one of us, and they still are, only closer to the gods now.
Anyone who needs to can come here and pray, any hour of the day.
We'll keep their day every year, on the day we lost them.
Nobody here will forget what they did, I'll see to that.
They'd laugh at all this, but they'd be glad of it too.
The council went no further, but nobody said we can't remember them.
They did what they did, and that's worth saying out loud.
We'll come here now and then and talk to them, saint or not.
They were the best of us, whatever anyone calls them.
Rest well, and thank you for everything.
A few words for them, and then we'll get on, as they would want.
{SAINT}: the council said it today, and I said the words myself, and my voice only shook once.
{SAINT}. It still sounds strange. It also sounds right.
I asked for it and they said yes. {DEAD} would have rolled their eyes at the fuss, and been pleased.
[known] {SAINT}, with {GOD} now. I hope they're looking after each other.
